title: Latency journeyboard: model+route p50/p95/p99 with streaming vs non-streaming split
creator: Emily Chen
description: Build a single ‘journeyboard’ dashboard that surfaces p50/p95/p99 latency by model and route, with explicit breakdowns for streaming vs non-streaming I/O modes. Goal: reduce time-to-root-cause for latency regressions by making IO-mode discrepancies and model-specific tails immediately visible to on-call and SRE. This ticket covers telemetry tagging, trace hook enrichment, metric derivation, and dashboard composition (panels + drilldowns).
background: We currently have many route/model latency panels scattered across boards; operators lose context when an incident shows high p99 because it’s unclear whether the tail is caused by streaming sessions or blocking generation paths. Prior work added route-level percentiles but lacked consistent io_mode tagging at ingestion and trace links. This work unifies those pieces into a coherent journeyboard and adds waterfall and cohort drilling for request-shape analysis.
success_criteria: Dashboard that lets users select model and route and immediately see p50/p95/p99 for streaming and non-streaming rows
Telemetry includes io_mode tag for every request metric and is present on spans (trace_id + span tags)
Percentile panels are powered by efficient histogram-based metrics; queries complete <5s for 30d window
On-call runbook references the board and shows actionable playbooks for streaming vs non-streaming regressions
Alert rule prototype: detect divergence where p99_streaming > p99_non_streaming by > 2x for 15m
implementation_notes:
- Telemetry: add 'io_mode' = [streaming, sync] tag on request metrics and as span attribute in tracing hooks. Ensure model_name, route_name, model_version are propagated. Update instrumentation libraries (python/java/go) to set these tags at the request ingress.
- Metrics pipeline: update ClickHouse rollups to keep histograms per (model,route,io_mode) keys. Create derived time-series for p50/p95/p99 using histogram_quantile on the bucketed histograms.
- Tracing: enrich top-level span with 'route' and 'io_mode' to enable direct jump from dashboard to traces. Add convenience trace links (tempo/ui/trace/<trace_id>) in panel tooltips.
- Dashboard UI: single-page journeyboard with top selector (model, route, time range). Left column shows summary KPIs; middle column shows p50/p95/p99 split table with sparkline; right column shows waterfall + example traces and cohort filters (request tokens, prompt size, concurrency). Add heatmap for distribution and tail explorer for p99 samples.
- Queries: prototype PromQL/SQL in comments below; ensure performance by limiting cardinality and pre-aggregating histograms.
queries_examples: ClickHouse example: SELECT histogramQuantile(0.95)(buckets) AS p95 FROM latency_histograms WHERE model='mpt-30b' AND route='/generate' AND io_mode='streaming' AND ts >= now()-INTERVAL 1 HOUR
Derived metric approach: precompute p50/p95/p99 at 1m resolution for top N model-route pairs and store as timeseries for fast dashboards
Trace link template: https://tempo.internal.redwood/trace/{{trace_id}} (add trace_id field to DB)
risks_and_mitigation: High cardinality if we attach free-form route or model tags: mitigate by canonicalizing route names and enforcing model whitelist for pre-aggregations
Dashboard query slowness for long time ranges: mitigate with 1m precomputed rollups and 7d/30d aggregated views
Missing io_mode on legacy clients: fallback classification heuristic (if streaming RPC used OR Content-Type: text/event-stream then label 'streaming') and flag for telemetry team to remediate
acceptance_criteria: All new telemetry events include io_mode, model_name, route_name
Dashboard accessible from Console -> Observability -> Journeyboard and has exportable CSV
PRs merged for instrumentation libraries and metrics pipeline (links in comments)
Ops runbook updated with example play for streaming-tail and non-streaming spike
